title: Naming 3D objects
goal: I can name 3D objects and count their faces.
teach: A 3D object is solid: it has length, width and height. Its surfaces are faces. A cube has 6 equal square faces. A cuboid (like a cereal box) has 6 rectangle faces. A sphere is a ball. A cylinder is like a tin. A cone is like an ice-cream cone. A pyramid has triangle faces that meet at a point.

ex.q: How many faces does a cereal box have?
steps: A cereal box is a cuboid.
Count the faces in pairs: top and bottom, front and back, left and right.

watch: A square is flat (2D). A cube is solid (3D). Do not mix up the names.

qs.text: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
qs.steps:
1. Rule: a 3D object has faces (flat or curved surfaces), edges (where two faces meet) and vertices (corners). A cube has 6 square faces. A cuboid (box) has 6 rectangle faces. A sphere is round like a ball. A cylinder has 2 flat circles and 1 curved surface. A cone has 1 flat circle and a point.
2. A cylinder has 2 flat circles: top and bottom.
3. So it has 2 flat faces (and 1 curved surface).

qs.text: How many vertices (corners) does a cube have?
qs.hint: 4 on top and 4 at the bottom.
qs.steps:
1. Rule: a 3D object has faces (flat or curved surfaces), edges (where two faces meet) and vertices (corners). A cube has 6 square faces. A cuboid (box) has 6 rectangle faces. A sphere is round like a ball. A cylinder has 2 flat circles and 1 curved surface. A cone has 1 flat circle and a point.
2. Top: 4 corners. Bottom: 4 corners.
3. 4 + 4 = 8 vertices

qs.text: How many edges does a cube have?
qs.hint: 4 on top, 4 at the bottom, 4 standing up.
qs.steps:
1. Rule: a 3D object has faces (flat or curved surfaces), edges (where two faces meet) and vertices (corners). A cube has 6 square faces. A cuboid (box) has 6 rectangle faces. A sphere is round like a ball. A cylinder has 2 flat circles and 1 curved surface. A cone has 1 flat circle and a point.
2. Top: 4 edges. Bottom: 4 edges. Upright: 4 edges.
3. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 edges
